newsitem.title: UK: Orange sees growth as losses widen.
newsitem.headline: Orange sees growth as losses widen.

text.p: Orange Plc , Britain's newest mobile telephone company, reported a bigger loss Tuesday in its first full year since it was floated on the stock market, but said subscriber numbers continued to show healthy growth.

Pretax losses in the year rose to 229.1 million British pounds ($367.4 million) from 140.5 million ($225.5 million) in 1995, while revenues jumped 171 percent to 619 million pounds ($993.6 million) , including acquisitions.

Analysts, who do not expect the company to become profitable at the operating level before 1998 because of heavy investments to build its network, had expected annual pretax losses of around 231.1 million pounds ($371 million).
Orange, hoping to build on a reputation for innovation, which has given it a 11.5 percent market share despite its late market entrance, said its customer base now topped 850,000.

Managing director Hans Snook said the company, which plans to reach 96 percent of the British population by the end of the year and hopes to win mobile licences in Greece and the Netherlands, was "ideally positioned for further growth."
Snook said he expected 40 percent of the British to use mobile phones in the next decade, up from 11.7 percent now.
